title: Everyday Grammar Challenge
seoDescription: Take a fun 80-question everyday grammar challenge covering proofreading, punctuation, clear sentences, word choice, agreement, and time clues.
pageTitle: Only 10% Can Pass This Grammar Challenge
summary: A practical staged grammar challenge about everyday writing mistakes, clear sentences, word choice, proofreading, and careful reading.

homepage.title: Can You Pass This Everyday Grammar Challenge?
homepage.summary: Simple writing mistakes are easy to miss. See how sharp your grammar really is.

footer.aboutText: This Everyday Grammar Challenge is designed for entertainment and self-testing. It is not an official school exam, language certification, employment assessment, or professional evaluation. The challenge uses simplified grammar, clarity, and proofreading questions for a quick writing-skills experience.

landing.quickStartText: Start with everyday sentences, then spot punctuation, word choice, clarity, agreement, and proofreading mistakes.

stageGroups.title: Grammar Warm Up
stageGroups.encouragement: Good start. The next round moves into everyday punctuation checks.

choices: Everyone is entitled to their opinion.
Everyone is entitled to there opinion.
Everyone is entitled to they're opinion.
Everyone are entitled to their opinion.
questions.explanation: Their is the correct word for possession here.

choices: Each student has a locker.
Each student have a locker.
Each students have a locker.
Each student having a locker.
questions.explanation: Each points to one student at a time.

choices: After putting the cake in the oven, Maria checked the timer.
After putting the cake in the oven, the timer was checked.
Maria checked the timer after the oven.
The timer checked Maria after the cake.
questions.explanation: The first version makes the action and person clear.

choices: The team will meet today.
The team will will meet today.
The team today will meet.
The team will today meet.
questions.explanation: The second sentence repeats one word.

choices: Lena walked to the gate yesterday.
Lena walks to the gate yesterday.
Lena walking to the gate yesterday.
Lena walk to the gate yesterday.
questions.explanation: The time word matches the action.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence? Please ___ the window.
choices: close
green
because
table
questions.explanation: Close is the action that fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence? The chair is ___ the desk.
choices: beside
quickly
blue
because
questions.explanation: Beside shows where the chair is.

choices: The bags are heavy.
The bags is heavy.
The bag are heavy.
The bags heavy.
questions.explanation: The first sentence matches more than one bag.

stageGroups.title: Punctuation Basics
stageGroups.encouragement: Nice work. The next round checks whether sentences feel complete and natural.

choices: Where is the green folder?
Where is the green folder.
Where is the green folder,
Where is the green folder
questions.explanation: A direct question needs a question ending.

choices: I packed rice, beans, and fruit.
I packed rice beans and fruit.
I packed, rice beans and fruit.
I packed rice, beans and, fruit.
questions.explanation: The first sentence separates the items clearly.

choices: If it rains, we will stay inside.
If it rains we will stay inside.
If, it rains we will stay inside.
If it rains, we will stay, inside.
questions.explanation: The first sentence separates the opening condition clearly.

choices: Sam asked, "Can I help?"
Sam asked "Can I help?"
Sam asked, "Can I help."
Sam asked "Can I help."
questions.explanation: The first sentence marks the spoken question clearly.

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains an unnecessary word?
choices: The meeting starts at noon.
The meeting starts starts at noon.
The meeting starts at noon today.
The meeting starts before noon.
questions.explanation: The second sentence repeats the idea of exact time.

choices: The bus arrived at noon.
The bus arrived at noon
The bus arrived, at noon.
The bus, arrived at noon.
questions.explanation: The first sentence has a clear ending.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would a proofreader approve?
choices: Neither answer is correct.
Neither answer are correct.
Neither answers are correct.
Neither answer be correct.
questions.explanation: Neither points to one answer at a time.

choices: The cup is on the shelf near the door.
The cup is somewhere in the room.
A cup is in a place.
The shelf has something on it.
questions.explanation: The first sentence gives the clearest exact location.

stageGroups.title: Sentence Sense
stageGroups.encouragement: Good focus. Now the challenge turns toward word choice and natural phrasing.

choices: Everyone brought their notebook.
Everyone brought there notebook.
Everyone brought they're notebook.
Everyone bring their notebook.
questions.explanation: Their is the correct word for possession here.

choices: The rain stopped, and the path dried.
The rain stopped, the path dried.
The rain stopped and, the path dried.
The rain stopped the path dried.
questions.explanation: The first sentence joins the two ideas clearly.

choices: The package arrived on Tuesday morning.
The package arrived recently.
The package arrived sometime.
The package arrived before.
questions.explanation: The first sentence gives the clearest time.

choices: The room was quiet before the meeting.
Before the meeting.
The room quiet before the meeting.
Was quiet the room before meeting.
questions.explanation: The first sentence is complete.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence? The path was ___ after the rain.
choices: wet
quietly
because
chair
questions.explanation: Wet describes the path naturally.

choices: The list of items is on the desk.
The list of items are on the desk.
The list of item are on the desk.
The list of items be on the desk.
questions.explanation: The sentence is about one list.

choices: The clock shows five o clock.
The clock shows shows five o clock.
The clock five o clock shows.
The clock shows five.
questions.explanation: The second sentence repeats a word.

choices: When Ben called Alex, Ben was already home.
When Ben called Alex, he was already home.
Ben called Alex because he was home.
He called Alex when Ben got home.
questions.explanation: The first sentence clearly says who was home.

stageGroups.title: Word Choice
stageGroups.encouragement: Solid progress. The next round checks everyday matching between words and meaning.

choices: Its color is fading.
It's color is fading.
Its' color is fading.
Its colour's is fading.
questions.explanation: Its shows that the color belongs to something.

choices: The report is short and clear.
The report is short clear.
The report short and clear is.
The report is clearly short clear.
questions.explanation: The first version uses natural wording.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct word?
choices: You're welcome to join us.
Your welcome to join us.
Youre welcome to join us.
Your'e welcome to join us.
questions.explanation: You're means you are.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct word?
choices: The second box is heavier than the first.
The second box is heavier then the first.
The second box is heavy than the first.
The second box then heavier than first.
questions.explanation: Than is used for comparison.

choices: Nora gave the keys to him.
Nora gave the keys to he.
Nora gave him to the keys.
Nora gave the keys he.
questions.explanation: The first sentence uses the natural form after to.

choices: The letter arrived this morning.
The letter arrived arrived this morning.
The letter this morning arrived.
The letter arrived morning this.
questions.explanation: The second sentence repeats a word.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is easiest to understand?
choices: The phone is on the chair by the window.
The phone is there near it.
It is on the thing by the window.
The chair has something near somewhere.
questions.explanation: The first sentence names the object and place clearly.

choices: A bouquet of flowers was on the table.
A bouquet of flowers were on the table.
A bouquet of flower were on the table.
A bouquet flowers was on the table.
questions.explanation: The sentence is about one bouquet.

stageGroups.title: Agreement Checks
stageGroups.encouragement: Good eye. The next round focuses on clear references and avoiding confusion.

choices: The keys are in the drawer.
The keys is in the drawer.
The key are in the drawer.
The keys in the drawer.
questions.explanation: The first sentence matches more than one key.

choices: One apple is on the plate.
One apple are on the plate.
One apples is on the plate.
One apple on the plate.
questions.explanation: The first sentence matches one apple.

choices: The workers arrive early.
The workers arrives early.
The worker arrive early.
The workers early arrives.
questions.explanation: The first version matches more than one worker.

choices: The cup and plate are clean.
The cup and plate is clean.
The cup and plate clean.
The cup and plate are cleans.
questions.explanation: The first sentence matches two items.

choices: The dog chased the ball because it rolled away.
The dog chased the ball because them rolled away.
The dog chased the ball because they rolled away.
The dog chased the ball because he rolled away.
questions.explanation: It naturally refers to the ball.

choices: The meeting started at nine yesterday.
The meeting starts at nine yesterday.
The meeting start at nine yesterday.
The meeting starting at nine yesterday.
questions.explanation: The action matches the past time.

choices: The table has four legs.
The table have four legs.
The tables has four legs.
The table four legs has.
questions.explanation: The first sentence matches one table.

choices: The file is ready now.
The file is is ready now.
The file ready is now.
The file is now ready.
questions.explanation: The second sentence repeats a word.

stageGroups.title: Pronouns And References
stageGroups.encouragement: Nice. The next round checks time clues and consistent actions.

choices: After Ana met Rosa, Ana smiled.
After Ana met Rosa, she smiled.
After she met Rosa, Ana smiled.
Ana met Rosa after she smiled.
questions.explanation: The first version makes the person clear.

choices: The teacher handed the paper to me.
The teacher handed the paper to I.
The teacher handed I the paper to.
The teacher paper handed to me.
questions.explanation: The first sentence uses the natural form after to.

questions.prompt: Which sentence adds information not given? Original: The boy carried the bag.
choices: The boy carried the heavy bag.
The boy carried the bag.
A boy carried a bag.
The bag was carried by the boy.
questions.explanation: Only the first sentence adds a detail about the bag.

choices: When the bottle hit the bowl, the bottle broke.
When the bottle hit the bowl, it broke.
When it hit the bowl, the bottle broke.
The bottle broke when it hit the bowl.
questions.explanation: The first version removes possible confusion.

choices: The guide gave us a map.
The guide gave we a map.
The guide gave a map us.
The guide gave map to us a.
questions.explanation: The first sentence uses the natural form.

choices: The red bag is mine.
The red bag is my.
The red bag mine is.
The red bag is me.
questions.explanation: Mine fits when no other word follows it.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence? The sign says the door is ___.
choices: closed
slowly
because
chair
questions.explanation: Closed describes the door.

choices: The train stopped at the old station.
The train stopped there.
It stopped at the place.
The old station had it stop.
questions.explanation: The first sentence clearly says what stopped and where.

stageGroups.title: Tense And Time
stageGroups.encouragement: Good timing. The next round becomes more like real proofreading.

choices: Yesterday, Mara laid the keys on the table.
Yesterday, Mara lay the keys on the table.
Yesterday, Mara lied the keys on the table.
Yesterday, Mara lain the keys on the table.
questions.explanation: Laid is used when someone puts something down.

choices: By the time we arrived, the rain had stopped.
By the time we arrived, the rain has stopped.
By the time we arrive, the rain had stopped.
By the time we arriving, the rain had stopped.
questions.explanation: The time order is clear and consistent.

choices: After I finished the report, I sent it to Lina.
After I finish the report, I sent it to Lina.
After I finished the report, I send it to Lina.
After finishing the report, it was sent to Lina.
questions.explanation: The first sentence keeps the time and action clear.

choices: The shop had closed before I reached the door.
The shop has closed before I reached the door.
The shop closed before I had reach the door.
The shop had close before I reached the door.
questions.explanation: The first sentence shows the earlier action clearly.

choices: Every Friday, the team reviews the notes.
Every Friday, the team reviewed the notes tomorrow.
Every Friday, the team review the notes.
Every Friday, the team reviewing the notes.
questions.explanation: The first sentence works for a repeated action.

choices: Neither the folders nor the box is on the shelf.
Neither the folders nor the box are on the shelf.
Neither the box nor the folders is on the shelf.
Neither the folders nor the box be on the shelf.
questions.explanation: The action word matches the closer item, box.

choices: The notice affects everyone in the room.
The notice effects everyone in the room.
The notice affecting everyone in the room.
The notice affect everyone in the room.
questions.explanation: Affects is the correct word here.

choices: The manager, after checking the list, found one error.
The manager, after checking the list found one error.
The manager after, checking the list, found one error.
The manager found, after checking the list one error.
questions.explanation: The first sentence sets the added detail apart clearly.

stageGroups.title: Proofreading Round
stageGroups.encouragement: Sharp reading. The next round brings trickier writing mistakes.

choices: The client asked for fewer changes this time.
The client asked for less changes this time.
The client asked for fewer change this time.
The client asked less changes this time.
questions.explanation: Fewer fits things that can be counted.

choices: The editor marked the line for review.
The editor marked marked the line for review.
The editor line marked for review.
The editor marked the review line for.
questions.explanation: The second sentence repeats one word.

choices: The report was clear; the summary was too long.
The report was clear; and the summary was too long.
The report was clear the summary was too long.
The report was clear, the summary was too long.
questions.explanation: The first sentence joins two complete ideas cleanly.

choices: Walking past the gate, Nora saw the delivery truck.
Walking past the gate, the delivery truck was seen by Nora.
Nora saw walking past the gate the delivery truck.
The delivery truck walked past the gate, Nora saw it.
questions.explanation: The first version makes the person doing the action clear.

choices: The team needs a plan, a budget, and a schedule.
The team needs a plan, a budget, and scheduling.
The team needs planning, a budget, and a schedule.
The team needs a plan, budgeting, and schedule.
questions.explanation: The first sentence keeps the list balanced.

choices: The meeting ended before noon.
The meeting ended ended before noon.
The meeting before noon ended.
The meeting ended noon before.
questions.explanation: The second sentence repeats a word.

choices: The assistant used a clean envelope.
The assistant used an clean envelope.
The assistant clean used an envelope.
The assistant used envelope clean.
questions.explanation: A is the natural word before clean.

choices: The note on the desk belongs to Priya.
The note, on the desk belongs to Priya.
The note on the desk, belongs to Priya.
The note on, the desk belongs to Priya.
questions.explanation: The first sentence does not split the main idea.

stageGroups.title: Tricky Writing Mistakes
stageGroups.encouragement: Almost there. The final round mixes everything together.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence? The change will ___ the schedule.
choices: affect
effect
affects
effected
questions.explanation: Affect means to change something.

choices: The letter was sent to Omar after Sara signed it.
Sara signed it after the letter was sent to Omar.
After it was signed, Omar sent Sara the letter.
The letter signed Sara after Omar sent it.
questions.explanation: The first version keeps the order and people clear.

choices: A list of names is on the desk.
A list of names are on the desk.
A list of name are on the desk.
A list names is on the desk.
questions.explanation: The action word matches list.

choices: Who is at the door?
Whom is at the door?
Who'm is at the door?
Whom's at the door?
questions.explanation: Who is used for the person doing the action here.

choices: The folder with the forms is missing.
The folder with the forms are missing.
The forms with the folder is missing.
The folder with forms missing are.
questions.explanation: The action word matches folder.

choices: Each of the boxes has a label.
Each of the boxes have a label.
Each boxes has a label.
Each of the boxes having a label.
questions.explanation: Each points to one item at a time.

choices: Please bring the file, the receipt, and the form.
Please bring the file the receipt and the form.
Please bring, the file the receipt and the form.
Please bring the file, the receipt and, the form.
questions.explanation: The first sentence separates the items clearly.

questions.prompt: Which sentence adds information not given? Original: The notebook is on the table.
choices: The notebook is on the table beside the lamp.
The notebook is on the table.
A notebook is on a table.
The table has a notebook on it.
questions.explanation: Only the first sentence adds a new detail.

choices: The office closed early; the staff went home.
The office closed early, the staff went home.
The office closed early; and the staff went home.
The office closed early the staff went home.
questions.explanation: The semicolon joins two closely related complete ideas.

choices: The manager's notes were on the desk.
The managers notes were on the desk.
The managers' note were on the desk.
The manager's note's were on the desk.
questions.explanation: The first sentence shows the notes belong to one manager.

choices: The package arrived late; however, the client was patient.
The package arrived late, however, the client was patient.
The package arrived late however the client was patient.
The package arrived late; however the client was patient.
questions.explanation: The first sentence handles the connector clearly.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is written most clearly?
choices: After reviewing the report, Maya approved it.
After reviewing the report, approval was given.
After reviewing the report, the approval was made.
After reviewing the report, the report was approved by Maya.
questions.explanation: The first sentence clearly names who reviewed the report.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would a proofreader approve?
choices: She enjoys reading, writing, and painting.
She enjoys reading, writing, and to paint.
She enjoys to read, writing, and painting.
She enjoys reading, to write, and painting.
questions.explanation: The first sentence keeps the list balanced.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct word?
choices: The speaker answered the question clearly.
The speaker answered the question clear.
The speaker answered the question clarity.
The speaker answered the question cleared.
questions.explanation: Clearly describes how the answer was given.

choices: Neither the manager nor the assistants were available.
Neither the manager nor the assistants was available.
Neither the manager nor assistants was available.
Neither manager nor the assistants were available.
questions.explanation: The action word matches the closer plural noun, assistants.

choices: The report was sent to Nina and me.
The report was sent to Nina and I.
The report was sent to I and Nina.
The report Nina and me was sent to.
questions.explanation: Me is the natural form after to.
